process_management.name: Process Management
process_management.content: Process Management is the part of an OS that handles creation, scheduling and termination of processes. It ensures the CPU is utilized efficiently and every process gets a fair chance to execute.

processes.name: Processes
processes.content: A Process is a program in execution. It has a Process Control Block (PCB) containing process state, program counter, CPU registers, memory info and I/O status. A process moves through states: New, Ready, Running, Waiting, Terminated.

cpu_scheduling.name: CPU Scheduling
cpu_scheduling.content: CPU Scheduling decides which process in the ready queue gets the CPU next. Goals include maximizing CPU utilization & throughput, minimizing waiting time, turnaround time and response time. Scheduling can be preemptive or non-preemptive.

fcfs.name: FCFS (First Come First Serve)
fcfs.content: FCFS executes processes strictly in the order they arrive in the ready queue. It is non-preemptive and simple to implement, but can cause the Convoy Effect where short processes wait behind long ones, increasing average waiting time.

sjf.name: SJF (Shortest Job First)
sjf.content: SJF selects the process with the smallest burst time next. It minimizes average waiting time among non-preemptive algorithms but requires knowing burst times in advance and can cause starvation of longer processes.

round_robin.name: Round Robin
round_robin.content: Round Robin assigns each process a fixed time quantum in a cyclic order. It is preemptive and fair, ideal for time-sharing systems. Very small quantum increases context-switch overhead; very large quantum behaves like FCFS.
